claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning potential with iterative retraining on high-fidelity ab initio data can accurately model both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed framework will capture vibrational contributions to free energies.
The proposed framework will capture anharmonic contributions to free energies.
The proposed framework will capture electron–vibration contributions to free energies.
Active learning can identify regions in which ML predictions deviate from high-fidelity AIMD.
Iterative retraining on the identified configurations will ensure coverage of vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects.
Local bonding environments, atomic clusters, and lattice distortions contain signatures of anharmonic vibrations and electron–vibration coupling.
Enhanced ML descriptors can encode the local structural signatures relevant to anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
Selective AIMD sampling combined with active-learning retraining will reproduce the full free-energy landscape.
Selective sampling will avoid exhaustive AIMD while preserving vibrational, anharmonic, and electronic contributions.
Avoiding exhaustive AIMD sampling will reduce computational cost.
The framework will provide approximately an order-of-magnitude speedup relative to explicit AIMD.
The framework will outperform TOR-TILD computationally.
Predicted free energies will be within a few percent of full AIMD results.
The method is applicable from near the melting point through fusion conditions.
Validation on elemental and binary metals can precede extension to multicomponent high-entropy alloys such as CoCrFeMnNi.
The approach is primarily validated in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Systems with ultra-strong anharmonicity or unusually complex electronic interactions may require additional refinement.
A decisive benchmark can compare solid–liquid free-energy differences, fusion observables, entropy corrections, errors, and runtime against explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
Failure to attain free-energy errors within a few percent of AIMD or approximately an order-of-magnitude speedup would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe initial validation on elemental and binary systems before extension to multicomponent alloys, whereas the boundary states that the approach is already primarily validated in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
